handbookNote: Source: official 'Nevada Driver's Handbook' (DMV 700, March 2024 edition), published by the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles. Retrieved directly from dmv.nv.gov: the DMV's handbook page at dmv.nv.gov/dlhandbook.htm links the current PDF at dmv.nv.gov/pdfforms/dlbook.pdf, which was downloaded via a direct HTTPS request with a standard browser User-Agent header (dmv.nv.gov's root domain returns a JS-redirect stub and a bare/non-browser request to some subpages 403's, but a UA'd request to the actual content pages and the PDF itself succeeded cleanly). Full text was extracted natively via pdftotext -layout (not OCR; minor ToUnicode CMap warnings during extraction did not affect the readable text) and archived with a retrieval-method header to temp/handbooks/nv/driver.txt (a new file, separate from this project's existing nv notary handbook file in the same folder). Exam mechanics were independently confirmed -- not guessed -- from a second official DMV source, the Nevada DMV's own 'Testing' page at dmv.nv.gov/dltesting.htm, which states verbatim under 'Knowledge (Written) Test': 'The Nevada knowledge test for a Class C, non-commercial license consists of 25 multiple-choice questions' and '80 percent or better is a passing score. The test will stop when you have reached 20 correct answers or six incorrect.' That gives a maximum of 25 items, an 80% (20-correct) passing threshold, with the test ending early at either 20 correct or 6 incorrect answers -- no time limit is stated on that official page or anywhere else searched, so this track is treated as untimed (not guessed as timed). Content depth: the March 2024 handbook is substantial (about 4,250 lines / 240KB of extracted text) with well-differentiated chapters on licensing/GDL and instruction-permit rules, seatbelt/child-restraint law, signs/signals/highway markings, right-of-way, speed and stopping-distance physics, freeway/HOV driving, turning/passing/parking rules, a distinctively detailed Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) chapter unique to this edition, special conditions (night, weather, flash floods, work zones, stopped-emergency-vehicle law), sharing the road (commercial vehicles/motorcycles/mopeds/school buses/bicycles/pedestrians), towing/trailering physics, insurance and financial-responsibility law, the demerit-point schedule, and Nevada's DUI penalty structure. This comfortably supported 275 distinct, grounded, non-repetitive multiple-choice questions across 19 topic buckets, every one traceable to a specific handbook section/page or to the dltesting.htm page cited above -- no invented facts, no filler.
